gen-gf-turret-road-gf-gudea: Round, pen-drawn letters that announce themselves from across the room. Turret Road sets the tone with parentheses-like curves, while Gudea follows in thread-thin curves and gaps you can see straight through.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-hanken-grotesk: Pen-drawn roundness with real swagger up top. What stands out is the shared single-weight line: Turret Road draws it bold, Hanken Grotesk bends it like wire with wide channels into each counter.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-host-grotesk: Host Grotesk lets its curves sweep open, contemporary and unfussy. Host Grotesk keeps lines moving smoothly, while Turret Road's round, parenthesis-like forms and unvarying pen line do the shouting.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-ibm-plex-sans-arab: Turret Road's pen-like line never changes weight, so its round forms skim along. And IBM Plex Sans Arabic, with its easily readable open apertures, keeps text going comfortably, line after line.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-ibm-plex-sans-deva: IBM Plex Sans Devanagari lets rope-loose curves run free, never knotting at the ends, under Turret Road's bold round heading. Reading on feels loose, modern and pleasantly unhurried, all the way down.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-ibm-plex-sans-thai: Turret Road cuts every round form at one engraver's depth, bold and commanding, never deeper in places. IBM Plex Sans Thai stays easygoing, its c ends pointing apart like pincers.
Turret Road feels like bent pipe cleaner, every round letterform bold and commanding, drawn in one constant line. IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped then lets its curves stay stubbornly open.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-kantumruy-pro: Turret Road's round forms read like open parentheses, bold and commanding. Kantumruy Pro settles beneath, its e opening clearly to the right and its letterforms free of hairlines or swells.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-koho: Commanding, round and pen-drawn, Turret Road hums at a constant line weight. And KoHo, a sans with wide c apertures, keeps things moving smoothly beneath that bold, flat hum.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-kosugi-maru: Commanding from the first word, Turret Road draws round forms in one line. Kosugi Maru reads like glowing neon tube, with stroke ends held far apart, so extended text feels uncluttered.
